page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.4xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 16 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, providing 16 vCPUs. The instance is configured with 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and operates on a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps under a KVM hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates a clear divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is weak, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25%, and single-threaded gzip compression rated in the bottom 10%. Conversely, multi-core benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU tests, consistently register in the average range. Memory bandwidth read and write speeds are average, though the overall Passmark memory score is weak.

The primary tradeoff of this instance lies in its low single-threaded execution speed and lack of local storage, which requires reliance on network-attached storage. However, the dedicated core allocation ensures stable multi-threaded execution without resource contention. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory density relative to vCPUs makes it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not demand high single-core CPU throughput or high-speed local disk I/O.

This hardware profile is suited for memory-intensive applications such as medium-sized databases, caching layers like Redis, and multi-threaded data processing tasks. It is also applicable for static web serving and moderate software compilation workloads where multi-core scaling can compensate for weaker single-core performance.
